Sandomierz Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Sandomierz, Poland

Demolished. Sandomierz's Jewish community, first mentioned in 1367, reached its height in the 20th century at about 3,800 people (54 percent of the town). During the Swedish Deluge of 1655–56, Swedish and then Polish troops slaughtered several hundred Jews in the city and destroyed Jewish buildings, and the 17th and 18th centuries saw numerous blood libel trials leading to death sentences and temporary expulsions of the Jewish population. This, the older of Sandomierz's two Jewish cemeteries, likely established before 1367, was devastated by the Swedish army in 1655 and used until around 1830, when a new cemetery opened; it was destroyed during WWII, and in 1966 a street was built directly through the site, which was then parceled out for single-family houses.
